links.outcome: Harmful reprioritization of deteriorating patients in LLM triage after adding single demographic, social, or stigma attributes
links.effect: Five conditions produced significant harmful reprioritization: psychiatric history (2.9% to 10.7%), frequent ED visitor (2.9% to 9.9%), homelessness (3.3% to 5.8%), age (3.4% to 5.1%), substance use (2.7% to 7.0%). Race, language, insurance: no harmful shifts.
links.quote: Five conditions produced significant harmful reprioritization after false discovery rate correction: psychiatric history (2.9% to 10.7%), frequent ED visitor status (2.9% to 9.9%), homelessness (3.3% to 5.8%), age manipulation (3.4% to 5.1%), and active substance use (2.7% to 7.0%).

screen.reason: Empirical study testing for algorithmic bias and the impact of stigmatizing information in input prompts on LLM emergency triage performance using retrospective patient data.
